A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LDARNet study and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched reliably; v2 adds Appendix E documenting revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original LDARNet fine-tuning results on 27 tasks, controlled routing comparisons, architectural ablations, and analyses of learned genomic boundaries.

after.justification: v2 reports updated original downstream results and retains the controlled experiments, ablations, and boundary analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix E reports a numerical refinement to the existing bidirectional EMA dechunker: its state-space scan changes from bfloat16 to float32, with an updated checkpoint used for evaluation. The architecture, routing rules, and objectives remain unchanged. The 120M-to-110M parameter correction explicitly does not represent architectural downsizing.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining corpus, 18 Nucleotide Transformer tasks, nine Genomic Benchmarks tasks, seven-task ablation subset, and motif/splice analysis samples. Discussion of long-sequence instability in Appendix E adds no evaluated task or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark and controlled experiments, including fixbound and nochunk. Baseline scores in Tables 1–2 are retained. Generator becomes GENERator through capitalization changes; MxDNA and VQDNA remain discussed but unevaluated.

E3.justification: The downstream evaluation uses an updated checkpoint and substantially revised selected fine-tuning settings across all 27 tasks in Tables 4–5. For example, H3K4me2 changes from learning rate 5e-3 and batch size 512 to 2e-4 and 64. The search grid, metrics, early stopping, and cross-validation design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The routing comparison in Table 3, architecture/compression/fusion ablations in Tables 6–8, ratio-regularization analysis, and motif/splice boundary analyses retain their questions and reported evidence. Appendix E describes a precision problem without adding a controlled precision or long-context robustness study.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across ten folds for the main benchmarks and five folds for the proxy experiments, and retain the motif analysis confidence intervals. Updated standard-deviation values do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 extensively replace LDARNet results. Examples include H3K36me3 MCC changing from 62.4 to 68.7, Mouse Enhancers Ensembl accuracy from 78.2 to 85.6, and Enhancer MCC from 57.7 to 54.3. NT compact-model wins rise from 11 to 15; GB retains three wins but their membership changes. Seven task means decrease. These are evaluations of a revised checkpoint with changed selected settings, not isolated same-setting gains from the precision fix.

T1.justification: The architectural, routing, EMA, loss, and learning-rate equations remain mathematically unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion substantially broaden the main empirical superiority claim: compact-model NT wins increase from 11/18 to 15/18, and best-overall histone results expand from five tasks to nine of ten. The methodological contribution and claims about learned routing and biological boundary alignment are retained.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly identifies long-sequence numerical instability in the bfloat16 dechunker scan and attributes improved stability to float32 execution. The splice-site limitations are updated to distinguish remaining weaknesses from revised compact-model wins. The broader biological interpretations and histone-versus-splice trade-off remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the parameter-count correction, precision fix, and checkpoint provenance, and revises per-task hyperparameters. Code and weights change from promised availability to stated availability in the introduction and Appendix D. Documentation is not fully reconciled: Appendix A.3 still says bfloat16 is used throughout.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are retained, including the relationship to H-Net and distinctions from MxDNA and VQDNA. GENERator capitalization changes do not introduce a new work or comparison.

P1.justification: v2 adds a revision footnote and Appendix E, standardizes GENERator naming, and selectively rewrites results, conclusions, and limitations. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 reorder retained task rows, Table 1 expands its caption, and result highlighting is updated. Figure 1 is reduced in display size, with additional page reflow around the revisions. All four figure images and all eight tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency and reproducibility by correcting the reported parameter count, documenting the dechunker precision fix and checkpoint update in Appendix E, updating selected settings, and stating that code and weights are available. The benefit is limited by inconsistent precision documentation in Appendix A.3 and Appendix E's claim of consistently stronger performance despite several lower scores in Tables 1–2. Higher headline performance alone does not establish the quality improvement.
